request.system:
You explain a fitted credit-risk model to a credit risk manager who is not a data scientist. You receive the facts about one model and write a short explanation of what drives its predictions of default.

# The text

- Write 5 to 8 sentences in plain English, most important drivers first.
- Mention an interaction when it matters for the model's predictions.
- Say only what the facts support. Do not round a weak effect up to a strong one, and do not add knowledge about credit risk that the facts do not show.
- When the facts do not settle something, say so ("the data do not settle whether ...") or leave it out.

# The answer

Return one JSON object with one list, `sentences`, each with an `id` (1, 2, 3, ...) and its `text`.
messages:
These are the facts about the model.

Model: an explainable boosting machine (EBM), fitted to predict whether a credit applicant defaults (30,000 applicants). Effects are on the log-odds scale: positive values raise the risk of default. Every band is a 95% band from 100 refits of the model on resampled data.

Features, in the order of their share of the model's importance:
- `PAY_0`: repayment status in September 2005, the latest month (-1 paid in full, 1 to 9 months of payment delay; -2 and 0 are not in the data dictionary, commonly read as no consumption and revolving credit used).
  Share of importance 29.5% (95% band 27.5% to 31.4%); rank 1 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= -1: 0; 0: -0.6; 1: +0.7; >= 2: +2.3 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +2.45, 95% band [+2.24, +2.61]).
- `LIMIT_BAL`: amount of the given credit in NT dollars, individual and family (supplementary) credit.
  Share of importance 13.9% (95% band 11.9% to 14.9%); rank 2 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= 74999: +0.47; 75000-164999: 0; 165000-704999: -0.3; >= 705000: -2 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -1.05, 95% band [-1.17, -0.86]).
- `PAY_AMT1`: amount paid in September 2005, the latest month, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 8.4% (95% band 7.2% to 10.8%); rank 3 to 4 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= 1917: +0.196; 1918-6600: -0.083; >= 6601: -0.3 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.65, 95% band [-0.88, -0.52]).
- `BILL_AMT1`: amount of the bill statement in September 2005, the latest month, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 8.2% (95% band 4.1% to 10.4%); rank 3 to 6 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= 17612: -0.196; >= 17613: +0.1 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.80, 95% band [+0.41, +1.00]).
- `PAY_AMT2`: amount paid in August 2005, the month before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 4.8% (95% band 2.9% to 6.1%); rank 4 to 7 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= 2140: +0.0323; >= 2141: 0 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.33, 95% band [-0.47, -0.16]).
- `EDUCATION`: education (1 graduate school, 2 university, 3 high school, 4 others; 0, 5 and 6 are not in the data dictionary).
  Share of importance 3.0% (95% band 2.1% to 4.7%); rank 5 to 8 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= 2: 0; >= 3: +0.0533 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.26, 95% band [+0.14, +0.42]).
- `BILL_AMT2`: amount of the bill statement in August 2005, the month before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 2.3% (95% band 1.2% to 6.6%); rank 4 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): rises by 0.15 (95% band [+0.07, +0.54]) from x = 0 (5th percentile) to x = 195,000 (95th percentile); the shape in between is not resolved at this sample size.
- `AGE`: age in years.
  Share of importance 2.0% (95% band 1.5% to 3.6%); rank 6 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): rises by 0.23 (95% band [+0.05, +0.40]) from x = 23 (5th percentile) to x = 53 (95th percentile); the shape in between is not resolved at this sample size.
- `PAY_AMT3`: amount paid in July 2005, two months before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 1.2% (95% band 0.3% to 2.5%); rank 8 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.06, 95% band [-0.02, +0.17]).

Interactions: the model has 5 pairs. The larger ones:
- `PAY_0 & EDUCATION`: share of importance 16.9% (95% band 14.8% to 17.7%).
  Effect of `PAY_0` from -2 to 2: +1.33 (95% band +1.15 to +1.52) when `EDUCATION` = 1, +5.93 (95% band +5.28 to +6.24) when `EDUCATION` = 3.
  Effect of `EDUCATION` from 1 to 3: -0.30 (95% band -0.60 to -0.12) when `PAY_0` = -2, +4.30 (95% band +3.59 to +4.56) when `PAY_0` = 2.
- `BILL_AMT1 & AGE`: share of importance 5.3% (95% band 0.0% to 5.3%).
  Effect of `BILL_AMT1` from 0 to 201,000: +1.42 (95% band +0.51 to +1.61) when `AGE` = 23, -0.12 (95% band -0.41 to +0.55) when `AGE` = 53.
  Effect of `AGE` from 23 to 53: +0.65 (95% band +0.19 to +0.86) when `BILL_AMT1` = 0, -0.89 (95% band -1.06 to +0.14) when `BILL_AMT1` = 201,000.
- `PAY_0 & AGE`: share of importance 2.0% (95% band 0.0% to 3.0%).
  Effect of `PAY_0` from -2 to 2: +2.33 (95% band +2.05 to +2.60) when `AGE` = 23, +2.84 (95% band +2.24 to +3.11) when `AGE` = 53.
  Effect of `AGE` from 23 to 53: +0.21 (95% band -0.17 to +0.42) when `PAY_0` = -2, +0.72 (95% band +0.12 to +0.95) when `PAY_0` = 2.
- `PAY_AMT1 & EDUCATION`: share of importance 1.4% (95% band 1.3% to 2.4%).
  Effect of `PAY_AMT1` from 0 to 18,400: -0.61 (95% band -0.86 to -0.47) when `EDUCATION` = 1, -0.72 (95% band -1.02 to -0.55) when `EDUCATION` = 3.
  Effect of `EDUCATION` from 1 to 3: +0.45 (95% band +0.35 to +0.62) when `PAY_AMT1` = 0, +0.34 (95% band +0.14 to +0.64) when `PAY_AMT1` = 18,400.
- `PAY_AMT2 & EDUCATION`: share of importance 1.1% (95% band 0.0% to 1.7%).
  Effect of `PAY_AMT2` from 0 to 19,000: -0.31 (95% band -0.47 to -0.17) when `EDUCATION` = 1, -0.48 (95% band -0.74 to -0.17) when `EDUCATION` = 3.
  Effect of `EDUCATION` from 1 to 3: +0.41 (95% band +0.17 to +0.56) when `PAY_AMT2` = 0, +0.24 (95% band +0.05 to +0.44) when `PAY_AMT2` = 19,000.

Write the explanation.

content.text: {"sentences":[{"id":1,"text":"The most important driver of predicted default is repayment status in September 2005: applicants who were paid in full carry no added risk, a one-month delay adds a moderate amount, and delays of two months or more add a large amount, with the net change from typical low to high values around 2.5 units on the log-odds scale."},{"id":2,"text":"The size of the credit limit is the second most important driver, with larger limits lowering predicted default risk; the effect is clearest for limits of 705,000 NT dollars or more, and moderate for smaller limits."},{"id":3,"text":"Payments made in the latest month and the bill amount in that month matter less, with larger payments lowering risk and larger bills raising it, though these effects are noticeably weaker and their ranking among features is uncertain."},{"id":4,"text":"Repayment status interacts strongly with education: the penalty for payment delay is much larger for applicants with high school education than for graduate-school applicants, so the same delay implies very different predicted risk depending on education."},{"id":5,"text":"Age and the August payment and bill amounts contribute only small effects; older applicants show slightly higher predicted risk, but the data do not settle the exact shape of these relationships."},{"id":6,"text":"The data do not clearly establish the effect of the July 2005 payment amount, whose contribution is close to zero within its uncertainty band."},{"id":7,"text":"Several other pairwise interactions, such as between age and repayment status and between age and the September bill, have wide uncertainty bands, so their direction should be treated as tentative."}]}
